name: Question 14
problem:
Which of the following equalities are true given that
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{4}\}.$

I. ${∬}_{D}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2}\,\text{d}A={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2}\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$$\,$

II. ${∬}_{D}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2}\,\text{d}A={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2}\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$

III. ${∬}_{D}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2}\,\text{d}A={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2}\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$
worked_solution:
We notice that:

- the limits for the variable $x$ are from $0$ to $\frac{\pi }{2}$, and

- the limits for the variable $y$ are from $0$ to $\frac{\pi }{4}.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\text{ }\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since the region of integration is rectangular, we can simply swap the order of integration. This gives

$$
{∬}_{D}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2}\,\text{d}A={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x.
$$

So, the correct answer is "I and III only".
